title: The Witness of Ashcombe
premise: Retired detective Sable Halloran, who quietly solved three deaths the police dismissed as accidents, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a prediction tied to Ashcombe's centenary gala. Following the client's cryptic ledger, hidden in the margins of books in his own failing bookshop, Sable uncovers a decades-old cover-up: the town's founding families buried a death in 1975 and have been paying silence ever since. The 'future murder' is retribution scheduled by the last living witness, now dying of cancer. In the end, Sable must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and exposing the truth, and he chooses truth — delivering the ledger to the one honest officer left, as the would-be killer, confronted with being seen at last, surrenders before the gala's final toast.
about_author: Lena Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing obituaries, court records, and unsolved mysteries. She writes quiet, character-driven mysteries about ordinary places hiding extraordinary secrets.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Sable Halloran, tending his failing bookshop, receives a stranger who pays triple to prove a murder will NOT happen — then vanishes. Sable's POV; beat of wary curiosity rekindling an old instinct he thought retired.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Remembered
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Sable's memory of the three deaths he solved off the record, establishing his methods and why he stays invisible. His POV; melancholy pride shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Margins and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Sable discovers pencil notations in secondhand stock matching the client's receipt — a ledger encoded across dozens of books. His POV; the thrill of the hunt returning like an old ache.

chapters.title: The Centenary Committee
chapters.summary: Sable attends a planning meeting for Ashcombe's 100th anniversary gala, observing the founding families' brittle courtesy. His POV; unease beneath civic warmth.

chapters.title: What Vera Kept
chapters.summary: Vera Ostrander, elderly town matriarch, warns Sable to stop asking questions — then slips him a torn photograph from 1975. Alternating POV with Vera; fear disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Drowned Year
chapters.summary: Sable digs into archives: a young woman, Elsie Marsh, died in the reservoir the year the dam was built; ruled accidental. His POV; cold anger at how neatly history was filed away.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Decoding accelerates: the ledger records annual payments from five families to an unnamed recipient — silence money, still active. Sable's POV; dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Honest Officer
chapters.summary: Sable cautiously approaches DS Imogen Reyes, the only police officer he trusts, testing her without revealing everything. Dual POV; mutual suspicion edged with respect.

chapters.title: Threats in the Stacks
chapters.summary: The bookshop is ransacked; specific ledger books are stolen but the code is distributed too widely to erase. Sable's POV; violation and defiance.

chapters.title: The Fifth Family
chapters.summary: Sable identifies four payer families but the fifth name is smudged — clues point toward someone unexpectedly close to him. His POV; betrayal's first bitter taste.

chapters.title: Elsie's Sister
chapters.summary: He finds Nell Marsh, Elsie's sister, living under another name — the recipient of the payments, and the client's mother. Nell's POV; grief worn smooth by fifty years of waiting.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Nell reveals her son Tomas hired Sable: she is dying, and she planned to kill Aldous Crane, the man who drowned Elsie, at the gala. Nell's POV; terrible tenderness and exhausted fury.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable weighs exposing Nell against letting justice happen outside the law, remembering every case the system failed. His POV; moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Crane's Version
chapters.summary: Aldous Crane, now frail and celebrated, hints he knows someone is watching him — and offers Sable money to find out who. Crane's POV briefly, then Sable's; revulsion at respected evil.

chapters.title: The Smudged Name
chapters.summary: Sable recovers the fifth family's identity: it was his own late mentor, whose estate still receives payments — explaining the client's knowledge of him. His POV; grief and self-doubt.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Bookshop
chapters.summary: With days left, Sable and Reyes reconstruct the gala plan from the ledger's final entries; Tomas realizes they know. Dual POV; tightening dread, reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: Drought lowers the reservoir, exposing evidence of Elsie's death — rope fragments, a locket. Sable's POV; the past literally surfacing, vindication and horror.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Centenary night: toasts, lanterns, and Sable moving through the crowd tracking both Tomas and Crane. His POV; coiled suspense.

chapters.title: Ash on the Water
chapters.summary: Tomas confronts Crane at the reservoir's edge; Sable intervenes, and Nell arrives to stop her son herself. Multi-POV climax; raw grief colliding with mercy.

chapters.title: Being Seen
chapters.summary: Confronted with witness and truth, Tomas breaks down and surrenders; Crane is arrested as the locket evidence lands with Reyes. Sable's POV; catharsis without triumph.

chapters.title: The Price of Truth
chapters.summary: Ashcombe reels; some families flee, others apologize; Nell dies peacefully weeks later knowing Elsie was named and mourned publicly. Reyes's POV; sorrow braided with relief.

chapters.title: Open for Business
chapters.summary: Spring: the bookshop reopens, a new mystery walks in, and Sable — no longer invisible — chooses to stay. His POV; quiet hope, the detective reborn in daylight.
